channel.title: Sir Reginald
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Sir Reginald" - A SCP that possesses people, but is unknowingly an entity from another reality

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded: Thank you so much for the critique! Like I said above, I mostly agree with the anomalous weapons thing, and the idea of the reality anomaly spreading throughout the world is a really interesting idea that I might expand on further. Now that I think about it, in terms of the a reality anomaly, it might be cool to make the "realness" of Sir Reginald dependent on the extent of the belief of others on his existence.

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded: Thanks so much for the critique! I agree that the anomalous weapon part is probably a bit redundant, so what kind of different anomalous properties would you advise the SCP have instead of the possessing and weapon thing?

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official critter here, but I can still read and give opinions.
So, I mostly agree with Grigori above. The idea is really cool, I personally love this kind of 'meta' stuff. But I would also recommend cutting out the anomalous weapon bit. I don't think the possession is a problem myself, it makes sense as a way for a fictional character to 'anchor' itself to our reality; but I think the anomalous weapons bit would simply make it look as though you're making it be more dangerous than it needs to be.
Not everything needs to be able to destroy a plane to be interesting.

This aside, I believe, another interesting concept you could explore instead- if you think the personal woes of Sir Reginald coming to terms with not being "real" are not enough- is how they got here at all, if that is still an active phenomenon/it can spread to other media, and what that means for whatever work Reginald is from originally.
Just a bunch of ideas, you're free to completely disregard them if you don't feel they're interesting enough for you.

Overall though, I really like this! Definitely gonna be reading it once it's written out as a draft and hopefully as a real Object!

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
I'm somewhat interested in a fictional character manifesting and having to deal with it's "unreality"

But the whole "it possesses people and takes over bodies" and "makes anomalous weapons" things seems less interesting.

My advice would be to cut out those two things and make him literally a physical manifestation of the fictional character, who at first is confused and then starts having to deal with the fact that he's a character from a tv show. That psychological conflict is enough to carry the whole article. The other two things would only feel like distractions.

item.title: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Action

Page Layout: Might include a journal written by the SCP later in the article's progression

Elevator Pitch: The SCP entity has the ability to passively possess any sentient beings within a certain radius upon the termination of the previous host. Upon possession, it will immediately overwrite the host's brain with the entity's personality. SCP-1 will also have an increase in intelligence/IQ scaling according to the intelligence of the host pre-possession (the smarter the host, the smarter SCP-1 is). SCP-1 is initially oblivious to the fact that they possesses people.

SCP-1 has an affinity to create advanced weapons. The dangerousness of the weapons also scale with the intelligence of the host. Due to this, the Foundation facilitates the containment of the entity by guaranteeing the termination of it’s previous host within suitable range of a “dumb” enough host. Foundation researchers theorize that given a smart enough host, SCP-1 could cause a XK-Class Scenario.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP is actually a character from a fictional universe in the SCP universe, who somehow got into the base SCP universe through a reality anomaly. The entity has a confused memory of its life, and is missing many details about itself.

Someone working the Foundation comments on the similarities they saw between SCP-1 and a character in a show that they watched as a kid to SCP-1, the entity is confused by the character's name, aggressively claiming to not be/know the character. The SCP slowly regains a sense of self awareness throughout the article due to this, slowly regaining memories and gradually realizing what it is, going insane.

The Foundation also is looking into utilizing its intelligence increase potential on Foundation employees to help create anomalous weapons that would help the containment of other SCPs.

Hook: The premise of a SCP slowly losing its mind due to it being foreign to the universe and its rules.

Additional Notes: The SCP’s original universe’s narrative is subject to change as I want to make its backstory integral to the narrative. I also want to add an experiment log with some of the creations SCP-1 has created during testing.

Would love to see any form of critique, but especially on how original the idea is and how interesting the idea is.
This is my first time doing an idea, so I appreciate everyone reading through it!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn
